assessment: Part 3 of a series, and the honest note is that the finished footage is short: 18:14 to 20:25, about two minutes, of which two stretches are comparison shots of the UPSTAIRS unit with the word upstairs burned into frame. Those are out, which leaves roughly a hundred seconds across nine camera setups. Enough for one Short and nothing spare. The countertop running into the window recess is the best single beat, and the stackable laundry is the one that sells it as an apartment rather than a finished basement. Cost slide after 21:00, fenced off.

project_context.summary: A basement turned into a self contained apartment. Full kitchen with a dishwasher, cabinets and countertop matching the upstairs remodel but a different backsplash, the counter carried into the window recess, a bathroom with a new deep tub and the same tile as upstairs, a resized vanity with the door shifted across, a stackable washer and dryer in a closet, and two bedrooms off the hall.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, cut entirely from 18:14 to 20:08, the finished apartment. No before footage, no progress footage, and nothing from the upstairs comparison shots.
notes: Every frame is the finished basement apartment.
The two 'upstairs' labelled stretches are excluded, they show a different unit.

shorts.full_vo: We just finished turning this whole basement into a self contained apartment. The kitchen cabinets and the countertop match the ones we did upstairs. Different backsplash, and it is a proper kitchen down here, dishwasher and all. Look how the countertop runs right into the window. So you get all that extra space behind the sink. The bathroom uses the same tile as the bathrooms upstairs. The tub is new, and it is a deep one. With a stone mosaic band running through it. And behind this door, a stackable washer and dryer. So whoever is living down here does their own laundry. Two bedrooms at the end of the hall, painted and carpeted. Its own kitchen, its own bathroom, its own laundry, and its own entrance.
